book_title:
The Holy Gospel of Jesus Christ
according to Luke.

intros.title: THE ARGUMENT OF S. LUKE'S GOSPEL.
intros.text:
S. Luke's Gospel may be divided into five parts.
The first part is, of the Infancy both of the precursor, and of Christ himself: chap. 1 and 2. The second, of the Preparation that was made to the manifestation of Christ: chap. 3 and a piece of the 4.
The third, of Christ's manifesting himself, by preaching and miracles, specially in Galilee: the other piece of the 4. chap. unto the midst of the 17.
The fourth of his coming into Jury towards his Passion: the other piece of the 17. chap. unto the midst of the 19.
The fifth, of the Holy Week of his Passion in Hierusalem: the other part of the 19. chap. unto the end of the book.
S. Luke was sectator (saith S. Hierome ) that is, a disciple of the Apostle Paul, and a companion of [1] all his peregrination. And the same we see in the Acts of the Apostles: Where, from the 16. chap. S. Luke putteth himself in the train of S. Paul, writing thus in the story. Forthwith we sought to go into Macedonia. And in like manner, in the first person, commonly through the rest of that book. Of him and his Gospel, S. Hierom understandeth this saying of S. Paul: We have sent with him the brother, whose praise is in the Gospel through all Churches. Where also he addeth: Some suppose, [2] so often as Paul in his Epistles saith, According to my Gospel, that he meaneth of Luke's book. And again: Luke learned the Gospel not only of the Apostle Paul, who had not been with our Lord in flesh, but of the other Apostles: which himself also in the beginning of his book declareth, saying, As [3] they delivered to us who themselves from the beginning saw, and were ministers of the word. It followeth in S. Hierome: Therefore he wrote the Gospel, as he had heard; but the Acts of the Apostles he compiled as he had seen. S. Paul writeth of him by name to the Colossians : Luke the [4] Physician saluteth you. And to Timothee : Luke alone is with me. Finally of his end thus doth S. [5] Hierome write: He lived fourscore and four years, having no wife. He is buried at Constantinople; [6] to which city his bones with the Relics of Andrew the Apostle were translated out of Achaia the twentieth year of ˹Constantinus˺. And of the same Translation also in another place against [7] [8] Vigilantius the Heretic: It grieveth him that the Relics of the Martyrs are covered with precious coverings, and that they are not either tied in clouts or thrown to the dunghill. Why, are we then [9] sacrilegious, when we enter the Churches of the Apostles? Was ˹Constantinus˺ the Emperor [10] sacrilegious, who translated to Constantinople the holy Relics of Andrew, Luke, and Timothee: at which the Devil's roar, and the inhabiters of Vigilantius confess that they feel their presence? His sacred body is now at Padua in Italy, wither it was again translated from Constantinople.

verses.text: <sc>BECAVSE</sc> many haue gone about to compile a narration of the things that haue been accomplished among vs:
according as they haue deliuered vnto vs, vvho from the beginning them selues savv and vvere ministers of the vvord:
it seemed good also vnto me hauing diligently atteined to al things from the beginning, to vvrite to thee in order, good <cr>[1]</cr> Theophilus,
that thou maist knovv the veritie of those vvordes vvhereof thou hast been instructed.

<cr>[1]</cr> There vvas in the daies of Herod the king of Ievvrie, a certaine Priest named Zacharie, of the <na>[2]</na> course of Abia: and his vvife of the daughters of Aaron, and her name Elizabeth.

notes.text: The Gospel vpon the eue of S. Iohn Baptist.

verses.text: And they vvere both iust before God, vvalking in al the commaundements and iustifications of our Lord vvithout blame,
and they had no sonne: for that Elizabeth vvas barren, and both vvere vvel striken in their daies.
And it came to passe: vvhen he executed the priestly function in the order of his course before God,
according to the custome of the Priestly function, he vvent forth by lot <cr>[1]</cr> to offer incense, entring into the temple of our Lord:
and <cr>[1]</cr> al the multitude of the people vvas <na>[2]</na> praying vvithout at the houre of the incense.

notes.text: We see here that the Priest did his dutie within, the people in the meane time praying without: and that the Priests functions did profite then, though they neither heard nor saw his doings.

verses.text: And there appeared to him an Angel of our Lord, standing on the right hand of the altar of incense.
And Zacharie vvas troubled, seeing him: and feare fel vpon him.
But the Angel said to him, Feare not Zacharie, for thy praier is heard: and thy vvife Elizabeth shal beare thee a sonne, and thou shalt cal his name Iohn:
and thou shalt haue ioy and exultation, and many shal reioyce in his natiuitie.
for he shal be great before our Lord: <na>[1]</na> and vvine and sicer he shal not drinke: and he shal be replenished vvith the Holy Ghost euen from his mothers vvombe.

notes.text: This abstinence foretold and prescribed by the Angel, sheweth that it is a worthy thing, and an acte of religion in S. Iohn, as it was in the Nazarites.

verses.text: and he shal <cr>[1]</cr> conuert many of the children of Israel to the Lord their God,

and he shal goe before him in the spirit and vertue of Elias: that he may conuert the hartes of the fathers vnto the children, and the incredulous to the vvisedom of the iust, to prepare vnto the Lord a perfect people. ⊢
And Zacharie said to the Angel, VVhereby shal I knovv this? for I am old: and my wife is vvel striken in her daies.
And the Angel ansvvering said to him, I am Gabriel that assist before God: and am sent to speake to thee, and to euangelize these things to thee.

And behold, <na>[1]</na> thou shalt be dumme, and shalt not be able to speake vntil the day vvherein these things shal be done: for-because thou hast not beleeued my wordes, vvhich shal be fulfilled in their time.

notes.text: Zacharie punished for doubting of the Angels word.

verses.text: And the people vvas expecting Zacharie: and they marueled that he made tariance in the temple.
And comming forth he could not speake to them, and they knevv that he had seen a vision in the temple. And he made signes to them, and remained dumme.
And it came to passe, after the daies of his office vvere expired, he departed into his house.
And after these daies Elizabeth his vvife conceiued: and hid her self fiue moneths, saying,
For thus hath our Lord done to me in the daies vvherein he had respect to take avvay my reproche among men.

because there shal not be impossible vvith God any word.

And vvhence is this to me, that the mother of my Lord doth come to me?
For behold as the voice of thy salutation sounded in mine eares, the infant in my vvombe did leape for ioy.

verses.text: Because he that is mightie hath done great things to me, and holy is his name.
And his mercie from generation vnto generations, to them that feare him.
He hath shewed might in his arme: he hath dispersed the proude in the conceit of their hart.
He hath deposed the mightie from their seate, and hath exalted the humble.
The hungrie he hath filled vvith good things: and the riche he hath sent away emptie.
He hath receiued Israel his childe, being mindeful of his mercie,
As he spake to our fathers, to Abraham and his seede for euer.

verses.text: And her neighbours and kinsfolke heard that our Lord did magnifie his mercie vvith her, and they did congratulate her.
And it came to passe: on the eight day they came to circumcise the childe, and they called him by his fathers name, Zacharie.
And his mother ansvvering, said, Not so, but he shal be called Iohn.
And they said to her, That there is none in thy kinred that is called by this name.
And they made signes to his father, vvhat he would haue him called.
And demaunding a vvriting table, he vvrote, saying, <cr>[1]</cr> Iohn is his name. And they al marueled.
And forthvvith his mouth vvas opened, and his tonge, and he spake blessing God.
And feare came vpon al their neighbours: and al these things vvere bruited ouer al the hil-countrie of Iewrie:
and all that had heard, laid them vp in their hart, saying, what an one, trovv ye, shal this childe be? For the hand of our Lord vvas vvith him.
And Zacharie his father vvas replenished vvith the Holy Ghost: and he prophecied, saying,

Saluation from our enemies, and from the hand of al that hate vs:

[1] The othe vvhich he svvare to Abraham our father,

And behold, an Angel of our Lord stood beside them, and the brightnes of God did shine round about them, and they feared with a great feare.
And the angel said to them, Feare not: for behold I euangelize to you great ioy, that shal be to al the people:

who vvas of Matthat, vvho vvas of Leui, vvho vvas of Melchi, vvho vvas of Ianné, vvho vvas of Ioseph,
who vvas of Matthathias, vvho vvas of Amos, vvho vvas of Naum, vvho was of Hesli, vvho vvas of Naggé,
who vvas of Mahath, vvho vvas of Matthathias, who vvas of Semei, vvho vvas of Ioseph, vvho vvas of Iuda,
who vvas of Iohanna, vvho vvas of Resa, vvho vvas of Zorobabel, vvho vvas of Salathiel, vvho was of Neri,
vvho vvas of Melchi, vvho vvas of Addi, vvho vvas of Cosam, who vvas of Elmadan, vvho vvas of Her,
vvho vvas of Iesus, vvho vvas of Eliézer, vvho vvas of Iorim, vvho vvas of Matthat, vvho vvas of Leui,
who vvas of Simeon, vvho vvas of Iudas, vvho was of Ioseph, vvho vvas of Iona, vvho vvas of Eliacim,
who vvas of <na>[1]</na> <alt>Melcha</alt>, vvho vvas of Menna, who vvas of Matthatha, vvho vvas of Nathan, vvho vvas of Dauid,

notes.text: Melca.

verses.text: <cr>[1]</cr> vvho vvas of Iessé, vvho vvas of Obed, vvho was of Booz, vvho vvas of Salmon, vvho vvas of Naasson,
vvho vvas of Aminadab, vvho vvas of Aram, vvho vvas of Esron, vvho vvas of Phares, vvho vvas of Iudas,
vvho vvas of Iacob, vvho vvas of Isaac, vvho vvas of Abraham, vvho vvas of Tharé, vvho vvas of Nachor,
who was of Sarug, vvho vvas of Ragau, vvho vvas of Phaleg, vvho was of Heber, vvho was of Salé,
<na>[1]</na> vvho vvas of Cainan, vvho vvas of Arphaxad, vvho vvas of Sem, vvho vvas of Noë, vvho vvas of Lamech,

notes.text: Beza boldly wipeth out of this Gospel, these wordes, who was of Cainan: though al the Greeke copies both of the old Testament & of the new, haue the wordes with ful consent. whereby we learne the intolerable saucines of the Caluinists, and their contempt of holy Scripture, that dare so deale with the very Gospel it self.

who vvas of Henos, vvho vvas of Seth, vvho vvas of Adam, vvho vvas of God.

chapters.summary: Iohn, to prepare al to Christ (as Esay had prophecied of him) baptizeth them to penance; 7. insinuating their reprobation, and the Gentils vocation, 10. teaching also and exhorting ech sort to doe their dutie. 15. That him self is not Christ, he sheweth by the difference of their two baptismes: 17. and saith that Christ wil also iudge his baptized. 19. Iohns imprisonment. 21. Christ being him self also baptized of Iohn, hath testimonie from heauen, 23. as he whose generation reduceth vs againe to God. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text: THE SECOND part: The preparation that was made to the manifestation of CHRIST.

verses.text: <sc>AND <cr>[1]</cr> IESVS</sc> ful of the Holy Ghost, returned from Iordan, and vvas driuen in the spirit into the desert,
<na>[1]</na> fourtie daies, and vvas tempted of the deuil. And he did eate nothing in those daies: and vvhen they vvere ended, he vvas an hungred.

notes.text: The Chuches fast of 40 daies (called Lent) commeth of this, & is an Apostolical Tradition. Clem. Constit. Apost. li. 5 c. 13. Hier. ep. ad Marcel. adu erro. Montani. Leo ser. 6 et 9 de Quadrages.

verses.text: And the Deuil said to him, If thou be the sonne of God, say to this stone that it be made bread.
And IESVS made ansvver vnto him, It is vvritten, [1] That not in bread alone shal man liue, but in euery vvord of God.
And the Deuil brought him into an high mountaine, and shevved him al the kingdoms of the vvhole world in a moment of time:
and he said to him, To thee wil I giue this vvhole povver, and the glorie of them: for to me they are deliuered, and to vvhom I wil, I doe giue them.
Thou therfore if thou vvilt adore before me, they shal al be thine.
And IESVS ansvvering said to him, It is vvritten, [1][2] Thou shalt adore the Lord thy God, and him only shalt thou [3] serue.

notes.text: See the Annot. in S. Matthew c. 4, 11.
λατρεύσεις.

verses.text: And he brought him into Hierusalem, and set him vpon the pinnacle of the temple: and he said to him, If thou be the sonne of God, cast thy self from hence downeward.
For [1] it is written, that [2] He hath giuen his Angels charge of thee, that they preserue thee:

notes.text: If the Diuel him self alleage Scripture against Christ, no maruel that Heretikes do so against Christs Church.

verses.text: and that in their hands they shal beare thee vp, lest perhaps thou knocke thy foote against a stone.
And IESVS ansvvering said to him, It is said, [1] Thou shal not tempt the Lord thy God.
And al the tentation being ended, the Deuil departed from him vntil a time.
<cr>[1]</cr><na>[2]</na> And <sc>IESVS</sc> returned in the force of the spirit into Galilee, and the fame vvent forth through the vvhole countrie of him.

notes.text: THE third part: of Christes manifesting him self by preaching and miracles, specially in Galilee.

verses.text: And he taught in their synagogs, and vvas magnified of al.
<cr>[1]</cr> And he came to Nazareth vvhere he vvas brought vp: and he entred <na>[2]</na> according to his custom on the Sabboth day into the synagogue: and he rose vp to reade.

notes.text: Our Sauiour vsed to preach in their Synagogues.

verses.text: And the booke of Esay the Prophet vvas deliuered vnto him. And as he vnfolded the booke, he found the place vvhere it vvas vvritten,
[1] The Spirit of the Lord vpon me, for vvhich he anointed me, to euangelize vnto the poore he sent me, to heale the contrite of hart,
to preach to the captiues remission, and sight to the blinde, to dimisse the bruised vnto remission, to preach the acceptable yere of the Lord, and the day of retribution.
And vvhen he had folded the booke, he rendred it to the minister, and sate dovvne. And the eies of al in the synagogue vvere bent vpon him.
And he began to say vnto them: That this day is fulfilled this scripture in your eares.
And al gaue testimomonie to him: and they <na>[1]</na> marueled in the vvordes of grace that proceded from his mouth, and they said, Is not this Iosephs sonne?

notes.text: He had a maruelous grace, and an extraordinarie force in mouing the harts of his hearers.

verses.text: [1] And he said to them, Certes you vvil say to me this similitude, Physicion, cure they self: as great things as vve haue heard done in Capharnaum, doe also here in thy countrie.

notes.text: The Gospel vpon Munday in the 3 weeke of Lent.

verses.text: And he said, Amen I say to you, that no Prophet is accepted in his ovvne countrie.

In truth I say to you, <cr>[1]</cr> there vvere many vvidovves in the daies of Elias in Israel, vvhen the heauen vvas shut three yeres and six moneths, vvhen there vvas a great famine made in the whole earth:
and to none of them vvas Elias sent, but into Sarepta of Sidon, to a vvidovv vvoman.
<cr>[1]</cr> And there vvere many lepers in Israel vnder Elisæus the Prophet: and none of them vvas made cleane but Naaman the Syrian.
And al in the synagogue vvere filled vvith anger, hearing these things.
And they rose, and cast him out of the citie: and they brought him to the edge of the hil, vvherevpon their citie vvas built, that they might throvv him dovvne headlong.
But he passing through the middes of them, vvent his vvay. ⊢
<cr>[1]</cr> And he vvent dovvne into Capharnaum a citie of Galilee: and there he taught them on the Sabboths.
And they vvere astonied at his doctrine: because his talke vvas in povver.
And in the synagogue there vvas a man hauing an vncleane Diuel, and he cried out vvith a loud voice,
saying, Let be, vvhat to vs and thee IESVS of Nazareth? art thou come to destroy vs? I know thee vvho thou art, the SAINCT of God.
And <sc>IESVS</sc> rebuked him, saying, Hold thy peace, & goe out of him. And vvhen the Deuil had throvven him into the middes, he vvent out of him, and hurted him nothing.
And there came feare vpon al, and they talked together one vvith an other, saying, VVhat vvord is this, that in povver and vertue he commaundeth the vncleane spirits, and they goe out?
And the fame of him was published into euery place of the countrie.
<cr>[1]</cr> And <sc>IESVS</sc> rising vp out of the synagogue, entred into Simons house. <na>[2]</na> And Simons vviues mother vvas holden with a great feuer: and they besought him for her.

notes.text: The Gospel upon Thursday in the 3. week of Lent. And upon Imber Saturday in Whitsunweek. And in time of mortality. See Mar. 8, 22. in margin.

verses.text: And standing ouer her, he commaunded the feuer, and it left her. And incontinent rising, she ministred to them.
And when the sunne vvas dovvne, al that had diseased of sundrie maladies, brought them to him. But he imposing hands vpon euery one, cured them.
And Deuils vvent out from many, crying and saying, That thou art the sonne of God. And rebuking them he suffred them not to speake, that they knevv he vvas Christ.
And vvhen it vvas day, going forth he vvent into a desert place: and the multitudes sought him, and came euen vnto him: and they held him that he should not depart from them.
To vvhom he said, That to other cities also must I euangelize the kingdom of God: because therfore I vvas sent.
And he vvas preaching in the synagogs of Galilee. ⊢

chapters.summary: Christ going into the Desert to prepare him self before his manifestation, ouercommeth the tentations of the Diuel. 14. then beginning gloriously in Galilee, 16. he sheweth to them of Nazareth his commission out of Esay the Prophet, 23. insinuating by occasion the Iewes his countrimens reprobation. 31. In Capharnaum his doctrine is admired, 33. specially for his miracle in the Synagogue. 38. from which, going to Peters house, he sheweth there much more power. 42. Then retiring into the wildernesse, he preacheth afterward to the other cities of Galilee.

verses.text: <sc>AND</sc> <na>[1]</na> it came to passe, vvhen the multitudes pressed vpon him to heare the vvord of God, and him self stoode beside the lake of Genesareth.

notes.text: The Gospel vpon the 4 Sunday after Pentecost.

verses.text: <cr>[1]</cr> And he savv tvvo shippes standing by the lake: and the fishers vvere gone dovvne, and vvashed their nettes.
And he going vp into one ship that vvas Simons, desired him to bring it backe a litle from the land. And sitting, he taught the multitudes out of the ship.
And as he ceased to speake, he said to Simon, Launche forth into the deepe, and let loose your nettes to make a draught.
And Simon ansvvering, said to him, Maister, labouring al the night, vve haue taken nothing: but in thy vvord I vvil let loose the nette.
And vvhen they had done this, they inclosed a very great multitude of fishes, and their nette vvas broken.
And they beckened to their fellovves that vvere in the other ship, that they should come and help them. And they came and filled both shippes, so that they did sinke.
VVhich vvhen Simon Peter did see, he fel dovvne at <sc>IESVS</sc> knees, saying, Goe forth from me, because I am a sinful man, O Lord.
For he vvas vvholy astonished and al that vvere vvith him, at the draught of fishes which they had taken.
In like maner also Iames and Iohn the sonnes of Zebedee, vvho vvere Simons fellovves. And <sc>IESVS</sc> said to Simon, Feare not: from this time novv, thou shalt be taking men.
And hauing brought their shippes to land, leauing al things they folovved him. ⊢

<cr>[1]</cr> And it came to passe, vvhen he vvas in one of the cities, and behold a man ful of leprosie, and seeing <sc>IESVS</sc>, and falling on his face, besought him saying, Lord, if thou vvilt, thou canst make me cleane.
And stretching forth the hand, he <na>[1]</na> touched him, saying, I vvil. be thou made cleane. And immediatly the leprosie departed from him.

notes.text: Our Saviour often healeth by touching.

verses.text: And he commaunded him that he should tel no body, but, Goe, <cr>[1]</cr> shew thy self to the Priest, and offer for thy cleansing <cr>[2]</cr> as Moyses commaunded, for a testimonie to them.
But the bruite of him vvent abrode the more. and great multitudes came together to heare, and to be cured of their infirmities.
And he retired into the desert, and praied.

<cr>[1]</cr><na>[2]</na> And it came to passe one day, and he sate teaching. And there vvere Pharisees sitting and Doctors of Lavv that vvere come out of euery tovvne of Galilee and Ievvrie and Hierusalem: and the vertue of our Lord vvas to heale them.

notes.text: The Gospel upon Imber Friday in Whitsunweek.

verses.text: And behold men carying in a bed a man that had the palsey: and they sought to bring him in, and to lay him before him.
And not finding on vvhich side they might bring him in for the multitude, they vvent vp vpon the roofe, and through the tiles let him dovvne vvith the bed into the middes, before <sc>IESVS</sc>.
VVhose faith vvhen he savv, he said, Man, thy sinnes are forgiuen thee.
And the Scribes and Pharisees began to thinke, saying, Who is this that speaketh blasphemies? Who can forgiue sinnes, but only God?
And when <sc>IESVS</sc> knevve their cogitations, ansvvering he said to them, VVhat doe you thinke in your hartes?
VVhich is easier to say, Thy sinnes are forgiuen thee: or to say, Arise, and vvalke?
but that you may knovv that the sonne of man hath povver in earth to forgiue sinnes (he said to the sicke of the palsey) I say to thee, Arise, take vp thy bed, and goe into thy house.
And forthvvith rising vp before them, he tooke that wherein he lay: and he vvent into his house, magnifying God.
And al vvere astonied: and they magnified God. And they vvere replenished vvith feare, saying, That vve haue seen maruelous things to day. ⊢
<cr>[1]</cr><na>[2]</na> And after these things he vvent forth, and savv a Publican called Leui, sitting at the Custome-house, and he said to him, Folovv me.

notes.text: The Gospel upon S. Matthew's eve. Septemb. 20.

verses.text: And leauing al things, he rose and folovved him.
and Leui made him a great feast in his house: and there was a great multitude of Publicans, and of others that vvere sitting at the table vvith them.
And their Pharisees and Scribes murmured, saying to his disciples, Why doe you eate and drinke vvith Publicans and sinners?
And <sc>IESVS</sc> answering said to them, They that are vvhole, neede not the Physicion: but they that are il at ease.
<na>[1]</na> I came not to call the iust, but sinners to penance. ⊢

notes.text: Christ came not to call those, who presume of their owne iustice, and that coumpt them selues to haue no neede of Christ.

verses.text: But they said to him, <cr>[1]</cr> VVhy doe the disciples of Iohn <cr>[2]</cr> fast often, and make obsecrations, and of the Pharisees in like maner: but thine doe eate and drinke?
To vvhom he said, Why, can you make the children of the bridegrome fast whiles the bridegrome is vvith them?
But the daies vvil come: and vvhen the bridegrome shal be taken avvay from them, then they shal fast in those daies.

And he said a similitude also vnto them, That no man putteth a peece from a nevv garment into an old garment: othervvise both he breaketh the nevv, and the peece from the nevv agreeth not vvith the old.
And no bodie putteth nevv vvine into old bottels: othervvise the nevv vvine vvil breake the bottels, and it self vvil be shed, and the bottels vvil be lost.
But nevv vvine is to be put into nevv bottels: and both are preserued together.
And no man drinking old, vvil nevv by and by. for he saith, The old is better.

chapters.summary: Hauing taught the people out of Peters ship, 4. he sheweth in a miraculous taking of fishes, how he wil make him the fisher of men. 12. He cureth a leper by touching him, and sendeth him to the Priest in witnesse that he is not against Moyses. 15. The people flocking vnto him, he retireth into the wildernesse. 17. To the Pharisees in a solemne assembly he proueth by a miracle his power to remit sinnes in earth. 27. He defendeth his eating with sinners, as being the Physicion of soules, 33. and his not prescribing as yet of any fastes to his Disciples.

verses.text: <sc>AND</sc> <cr>[1]</cr> it came to passe on the <na>[2]</na> Sabboth second-first, vvhen he passed through the corne, his Disciples did plucke the eares, and did eate rubbing them vvith their hands.

notes.text: S. Hierom (ep. 2 ad Nepotian.) writeth of him self, that being at Constantinople, he asked his maister Gregorie Nazianzene, the famous Doctor, then Bishop there, what Sabboth this was. who by his answer declared that it was very hard to tel, neither is it yet knowen to the best learned. Yet the Protestants are wont to say, Al is very easie.

verses.text: And certaine of the Pharisees said to them, VVhy doe you that vvhich is not lawful on the Sabboths?
And <sc>IESVS</sc> ansvvering them, said, Neither this haue you read vvhich Dauid did, vvhen him self vvas an hungred and they that vvere vvith him:

<cr>[1]</cr> hovv he entred into the house of God, and tooke the loaues of Proposition, and did eate, and gaue to them that vvere vvith him, vvhich it is not lavvful to eate <cr>[2]</cr> but only for Priests?
And he said to them, That the sonne of man is Lord of the Sabboth also.
And it came to passe on an other Sabboth also, that he entred into the synagogue, and taught. <cr>[1]</cr> And there vvas a man, and his right hand vvas vvithered.
And the Scribes and Pharisees vvatched if he vvould cure on the Sabboth: that they might finde hovv to accuse him.
But he knevv their cogitations: and he said to the man that had the withered hand, Arise, and stand forth into the middes. And rising he stoode.
And <sc>IESVS</sc> said to them, I aske you, if it be lavvful on the Sabboths to doe vvel or il: to saue a soule or to destroy?
And looking about vpon them al, he said to the man, Stretch forth thy hand. And he stretched it forth: and his hand vvas restored.
And they vvere replenished vvith madnes: and they communed one with an other what they might doe to <sc>IESVS</sc>.
<na>[1]</na> And it came to passe in those daies, he vvent forth into the mountaine to pray, and he passed the vvhole night in the prayer of God.

notes.text: The Gospel upon S. Bartholomew's day. Aug. 24.

verses.text: [1] And vvhen day vvas come, he called his Disciples: and he chose tvvelue of them ( vvhom also he named Apostles)
Simon vvhom he surnamed Peter, and Andrevv his brother, Iames and Iohn, Philippe and Bartholomew,
Matthevv and Thomas, Iames of Alphæus and Simon that is called Zelótes,
and Iude of Iames, and Iudas Iscariote vvhich vvas the traitour.

<na>[1]</na> And descending vvith them he stoode in a plaine place, and the multitude of his Disciples, and a very great companie of people from al Ievvrie and Hierusalem: and the sea coast both of Tyre and Sidon,

notes.text: The Gospel upon SS. Fabian and Sebastian's day, Ian. 20. upon S. Dionyse day. Octo. 9. upon Allhallows' eve. And for many Martyrs.

verses.text: which vvere come to heare him, and to be healed of their maladies. And they that vvere vexed of vncleane spirits, vvere cured.
And al the multitude <cr>[1]</cr> sought to touch him, because vertue vvent forth from him, and healed al. ⊢
And he lifting vp his eies vpon his Disciples, said, <cr>[1]</cr> Blessed are ye poore: for yours is the kingdom of God.
Blessed are you that novv are an hungred: because you shal be filled. Blessed are you that novv doe vveepe: because you shal laugh.
Blessed shal you be vvhen men shal hate you, and vvhen they shal separate you, and vpbraide you, and abandon your name as euil, for the sonne of mans sake.
Be glad in that day and reioyce: for behold, your revvard is much in heauen. ⊢ for according to these things did their fathers to the Prophets.
But wo to you that are riche, because you haue your consolation.
VVo to you that are filled: because you shal be hungrie. VVo to you that novv doe laugh: because you shal mourne and vveepe.
VVo, vvhen al men shal blesse you. for according to these things did their fathers to the false-Prophets.
But to you I say that doe heare, Loue your enemies, doe good to them that hate you.
Blesse them that curse you, and pray for them that calumniate you.
And he that striketh thee on the cheeke, offer also the other. And from him that taketh avvay from thee thy robe, prohibit not thy coate also.
And <na>[1]</na> to euery one that asketh thee, giue: and of him that taketh avvay the things that are thine, aske not againe.

notes.text: That is, to euery one iustly asking. For that which is vniustly asked, may be iustly denied. Aug. li. 1. c. 40. de Serm. Do. in monte.

verses.text: And according as you vvil that men doe to you, doe you also to them in like maner.
And if you loue them that loue you, vvhat thanke is to you? for sinners also loue those that loue them.
And if ye doe good to them that doe you good: vvhat thanke is to you? for sinners also doe this.
And if ye lend to them of vvhom ye hope to receiue: vvhat thanke is to you? for sinners also lend vnto sinners, for to receiue as much.

But loue ye your enemies: doe good and lend, hoping for nothing thereby, and your reward shal be much, and you shal be the sonnes of the Highest, because him self is beneficial vpon the vnkinde and the euil.
<na>[1]</na> Be ye therfore merciful as also your father is merciful.

notes.text: The Gospel vpon the first Sunday after Pentecost.

verses.text: Iudge not, & you shal not be iudged. condemne not, & you shal not be condemned. forgiue, and you shal be forgiuen.

Giue, and there shal be giuen to you. good measure & pressed dovvne and shaken together and running ouer shal they giue into your bosome. For vvith the same measure that you do meate, it shal be measured to you againe.
And he said to them a similitude also: Can the blinde leade the blinde? doe not both fal into the ditch?
The disciple is not aboue his maister: but euery one shal be perfect, if he be as his maister.
And vvhy seest thou the mote in thy brothers eie: but the beame that is in thine ovvne eie thou considerest not?

Or hovv canst thou say to thy brother, Brother, let me cast out the mote out of thine eie: thy self not seeing the beame in thine ovvne eie? Hypocrite, cast first the beame out of thine ovvne eie: and then shalt thou see clerely to take forth the mote out of thy brothers eie. ⊢
For there is no good tree that yeldeth euil fruites: nor euil tree, that yeldeth good fruite.
For euery tree is knovven by his fruite. For neither doe they gather figges of thornes: neither of a bush doe they gather the grape.
The good man of the good treasure of his hart bringeth forth good: and the euil man of the il treasure bringeth forth euil. for of the aboundance of the hart the mouth speaketh.
And vvhy cal you me, Lord, Lord: and doe not the things vvhich I say?
Euery one that commeth to me, and heareth my vvords, and doeth them: I vvil shevv you to vvhom he is like.

He is like to a man <na>[1]</na> building a house, that digged deepe, and laid the foundation vpon a rocke. And vvhen an inundation rose, the riuer bette against that house, and it could not moue it: for it vvas founded vpon a rocke.

notes.text: He buildeth right & surely, that hath both faith and good workes: he buildeth on sand, that trusteth to his faith or reading or knowledge of the scripture, and doth not worke or liue accordingly.

verses.text: But he that heareth, and doeth not: is like to a man building his house vpon the earth vvithout a foundation: against the vvhich the riuer did beate: and incontinent it fell, and the ruine of that house vvas great.

chapters.summary: For reprouing by Scripture and miracle (as also by reason) the Pharisees blindnes about the obseruation of the Sabboth, 11. they seeke his death. 12. Hauing in the mountaine prayed al night, he chooseth twelue Apostles. 17. and after many miracles vpon the diseased, 20. he maketh a sermon to his Disciples before the people: proposing heauen to such as wil suffer for him, 24. and wo to such as wil not. 27. Yet withal exhorting to doe good euen to our enemies also. 19. and that the Maisters must first mend them selues. 46. finally, to doe good workes, because only faith wil not suffice.

verses.text: <sc>AND</sc> <cr>[1]</cr> vvhen he had fully said al his vvords into the eares of the people, he entred into Capharnaum.
And the seruant of a certaine Centurion being sicke, vvas readie to die: vvho vvas deere vnto him.
And when he had heard of <sc>IESVS</sc>, he sent vnto him the Auncients of the Ievves, desiring him to come and heale his seruant.
But they being come to <sc>IESVS</sc>, besought him earnestly, saying to him, That he is vvorthie that thou shouldest doe this for him.
for he loueth our nation: and he hath built a synagogue for vs.

And IESVS went with them. And vvhen he was novv not farre from the house, the Centurion sent his frends vnto him, saying, Lord, trouble not thy self. for [1] I am not vvorthie that thou shouldest enter vnder my roofe.

notes.text: See the Annotations vpon S. Matth. c. 8, 8.

verses.text: for the vvhich cause neither did I thinke my self vvorthie to come to thee: but say the vvord, and my seruant shal be made whole.
for I also am a man subiect to authoritie, hauing vnder me souldiars: and I say to this, goe, and he goeth: and to an other, come, and he commeth: and to my seruant, doe this, and he doeth it.
Which <sc>IESVS</sc> hearing, marueiled: and turning to the multitudes that folovved him he said, Amen I say to you, neither in Israel haue I found so great faith.
And they that were sent, being returned home, found the seruant that had been sicke, whole.
<na>[1]</na> And it came to passe, aftervvard he vvent into a citie that is called Naim: and there vvent vvith him his Disciples and a very great multitude.

notes.text: The Gospel vpon the 15 Sunday after Pentecost. And vpon Thursday in the 4 weeke of Lent. And for S. Monica S. Augustins mother Maij. 4.

verses.text: And vvhen he came nigh to the gate of the citie, behold a dead man vvas caried forth, the only sonne of his mother: and she, vvas a vvidovv: and a great multitude of the citie vvith her.
Whom vvhen our Lord had seen, being moued vvith mercie vpon her, he said to her, VVeepe not.
And he came neere and touched the coffin. And they that caried it, stood stil: and he said, Yong man, I say to thee, Arise.
And he that vvas dead, sate vp, and beganne to speake. And he gaue him to his mother.
And feare tooke them al: and they magnified God, saying, That a great Prophet is risen among vs: and, That God hath visited his people.
And this saying vvent forth into al Ievvrie of him, and into al the countrie about.
And Iohns disciples shevved him of al these things.
<cr>[1]</cr> And Iohn called tvvo of his disciples, and sent them to <sc>IESVS</sc>, saying, Art thou he that art to come: or expect vve an other?
And vvhen the men vvere come vnto him, they said, Iohn the Baptist hath sent vs to thee, saying, Art thou he that art to come: or expect vve an other?
(And the self same houre, he cured many of maladies, and hurtes, and euil spirits: and to many blinde he <na>[1]</na> cgaue sight.)

notes.text: c ἐχαρίσατο.

verses.text: And answering, he said to them, Goe and report to Iohn vvhat you haue heard and seen: <cr>[1]</cr> That the blinde see, the lame walke, the lepers are made cleane, the deafe heare, the dead rise againe,
<na>[1]</na> the poore are euangelized: and blessed is he vvhosoeuer shal not be scandalized in me.

notes.text: Pauperes euangelizantur, that is, to the poore the Gospel is preached, and they receiue it.

verses.text: <cr>[1]</cr> And when Iohns messengers vvere departed, he began to say of Iohn to the multitudes, VVhat vvent you out into the desert to see? a reede moued vvith the vvinde?
But vvhat vvent you forth to see? a man clothed in <na>[1]</na> soft garments? behold they that are in costly apparel and delicacies, are in the house of kings.

notes.text: Marke this wel concerning Iohns apparel and diet. See the Annotations vpon S. Matth. c. 3, 4.

verses.text: But what vvent you out for to see? a Prophet? Certes I say to you, and more then a Prophet.
this is he of vvhom it is vvritten, [1] Behold I send mine Angel before thy face, vvhich shal prepare thy vvay before thee.
For I say to you, A greater Prophet among the children of vvomen then Iohn the Baptist, there is no man. but he that is the lesser in the kingdom of God, is greater then he.
And al the people hearing and the Publicans, iustified God, being baptized vvith Iohns baptisme.
But the Pharisees and the lavvyers <na>[1]</na> despised the counsel of God against them selues, being not baptized of him.

notes.text: As they that contēned Iohns baptisme, despised Gods counsel and wisedō: so much more they that make no accoumpt of the Sacraments of the Church, despise Gods counsel and ordinance touching their saluation, to their owne damnation.

verses.text: And our Lord said, VVherevnto then shal I liken the men of this generation, and vvherevnto are they like?
They are like to children sitting in the market-place, and speaking one to an other, and saying, VVe haue piped to you, and you haue not daunced: vve haue lamented, and you haue not vvept.
For Iohn the Baptist came <cr>[1]</cr> neither eating bread nor drinking vvine: and you say, He hath a deuil.
The sonne of man came eating and drinking: and you say, Behold a man that is a gurmander and a drinker of vvine, a frende of Publicans and sinners.
And vvisedom is iustified of al her children.
<na>[1]</na> And one of the Pharisees desired him to eate vvith him. And being entred into the house of the Pharisee, he sate downe to meate.

notes.text: The Gospel vpon S. Marie Magdalens day Iul. 22. And vpon Thursday in Passion weeke. And vpon Imber Friday in Sept.

verses.text: And behold a vvoman that was in the citie, a sinner, as she knevv that he vvas set downe in the Pharisees house, she brought an alabaster boxe of ointment:
and standing behind beside his feete, she began to <na>[1]</na> vvater his feete vvith teares, & vviped them vvith the heares of her head, and kissed his feete, & anointed them with the ointment.

notes.text: A perfect paterne of true penance in this woman, who sought of Christ with open teares & other strange workes of satisfaction and deuotion, remission of her sinnes.

verses.text: And the Pharisee that had bid him, seeing it, spake vvithin him self, saying, This man if he vvere a Prophet, vvould know certes vvho and vvhat maner of woman she is vvhich toucheth him, that she is a sinner.
And <sc>IESVS</sc> answering said to him, Simon, I haue somevvhat to say vnto thee. but he said, Maister, say.
A certaine creditour had tvvo debters: one did ovve fiue hundred pence, and the other fiftie.
They hauing not vvherevvith to pay, he forgaue both. VVhether therfore doth loue him more?
Simon answering said, I suppose that he to vvhom he forgaue more. But he said to him, Thou hast iudged rightly.

And turning to the vvoman, he said vnto Simon, Doest thou see this vvoman? I entred into thy house, vvater to my feete thou didst not giue: but she vvith teares hath vvatered my feete, and vvith her heares hath vviped them.
Kisse thou gauest me not: but she since I came in, hath not ceased to kisse my feete.
VVith oile thou didst not anoint my head: but she vvith ointment hath anointed my feete.
For the vvhich I say to thee, Many sinnes are forgiuen her, because she hath <na>[1]</na> loued much. But to vvhom lesse is forgiuen, he loueth lesse.

notes.text: Not only faith (as you may perceiue) but loue or charitie obtaineth remission of sinnes.

verses.text: And he said to her, Thy sinnes are forgiuen thee.
And they that sate together at the table, began to say within them selues, <na>[1]</na> Who is this that also forgiueth sinnes?

notes.text: As the Pharisees did alwaies carpe Christ for remission of sinnes in earth, so the Heretikes reprehend his Church that remitteth sinnes by his authoritie.

verses.text: And he said to the woman, Thy faith hath made the safe, goe in peace. ⊢

chapters.summary: He testifieth, the faith of the Centurion who was a Gentil, to be greater then he found among al the Iewes, and cureth his seruant absent. 11. the widowes sonne he reuiueth and restoreth to her, and is renowmed therevpon. 18. To Iohns messengers he answereth with miracles, leauing to Iohn to preach thereby vnto them that he is Christ. 24. And afterward he declareth how worthy credit was Iohns testimonie, 29. inueighing against the Pharisees, 31. who with neither of their maners of liuing could be wonne. 36. shewing also vnto them by occasion of Marie Magdalen, how he is a frende to sinners, not to maintaine them in sinne, but to forgiue them their sinnes vpon their faith and penance.

verses.text: <sc>AND</sc> it came to passe afterward, and he made his iourney by cities and tovvnes preaching and euangelizing the kingdom of God: and the Tvvelue vvith him,
and some vvomen that had been cured of wicked spirits and infirmities, <cr>[1]</cr> Marie vvhich is called Magdalene, out of whom seuen deuils vvere gone forth,
and Ioane the vvife of Chusa Herods procurator, and Susan, and <na>[1]</na> cmany others that did minister vnto him of their substance.

notes.text: aliæ multæ

verses.text: <cr>[1]</cr> And <na>[2]</na> vvhen a very great multitude assembled, and hastened out of the cities vnto him, he said by a similitude.

notes.text: The Gospel vpon the Sunday of Sexagesme.

verses.text: The sovver vvent forth to sovv his seede. and vvhiles he soweth, some fel by the vvay side, and vvas troden vpon, and the foules of the aire did eate it.
And other some fel vpon the rocke: and being shot vp, it withered, because it had not moisture.
And othersome fel among thornes, and the thornes grovving vp vvithal, choked it.
And other some fel vpon good ground: and being shot vp, yelded fruite an hundred fold. Saying these things he cried, He that hath eares to heare, let him heare.
And his disciples asked him vvhat this parable was.
To vvhom he said, To you it is giuen to knovv the mysterie of the kingdom of God, but to the rest in parables, <cr>[1]</cr> that <na>[2]</na> seeing they may not see, and hearing may not vnderstand.

notes.text: See the Annotations vpon S. Matthew. c. 13, 14.

verses.text: And the parable is this: The seede, is the vvord of God.
And they besides the vvay: are those that heare, then the deuil commeth, and taketh the vvord out of their hart, lest beleeuing they be saued.
For they vpon the rocke: such as vvhen they heare, vvith ioy receiue the vvord: and these haue no rootes: because <na>[1]</na> for a time they beleeue, and in time of tentation they reuolt.

notes.text: Against the Heretikes that say, faith once had can not be lost, and that he which now hath not faith, neuer had.

verses.text: And that vvhich fel into thornes, are they that haue heard, and going their vvaies, are choked vvith cares and riches and pleasures of this life, and render not fruite.
And that vpon good ground: are they vvhich in a good and very good hart, hearing the vvord, doe reteine it, and yeld fruite in patience. ⊢
And no man lighting a candel doth couer it vvith a vessel, or put it vnder a bed: but setteth it vpon a candelsticke, that they that enter in, may see the light.
For there is not any thing secrete, that shal not be made manifest: nor hid, that shal not be knowen, & come abrode.
See therfore how you heare. For he that hath, to him shal be giuen: and vvhosoeuer hath not, that also vvhich he thinketh he hath, shal be taken avvay from him.
And <cr>[1]</cr> his mother and brethren came vnto him: and they could not come at him for the multitude.
And it vvas told him, Thy mother and thy brethren stand vvithout, desirous to see thee.
Who ansvvering said to them, My <na>[1]</na> mother and my brethren, are they that heare the vvord of God and doe it.

notes.text: He did not here disdainfully speake of his mother, but teacheth that our spiritual kinred is to be preferred before carnal cognation. Hilar. in 12 Mat.

verses.text: <cr>[1]</cr> And it came to passe one day: and he vvent vp into a boate, and his disciples, and he said to them, Let vs strike ouer the lake. And they launched forth.
And when they vvere sailing, he slept: and there fel a storme of vvinde into the lake, and they <na>[1]</na> cvvere filled, and vvere in danger.

notes.text: c complebantur.

verses.text: And <na>[1]</na> they came and raised him, saying, Maister, vve perish. But he rising, rebuked the vvinde and the tempest of vvater: and it ceased, and there vvas made a calme.

notes.text: See the Annotations vpon S. Matthew c. 8, 24.

verses.text: And he said to them, VVhere is your faith? Who fearing, marueiled one to an other, saying, VVho is this (trovv ye) that he commaundeth both the vvindes and the sea, and they obey him?
<cr>[1]</cr> And they sailed to the countrie of the Gerasens vvhich is ouer against Galilee.
And vvhen he vvas come forth to the land, there mette him a certaine man that had a deuil novv a very long time, and he did vveare no clothes, neither did he tarie in house, but in the monuments.
And as he saw <sc>IESVS</sc>, he fel downe before him: and crying out vvith a great voice, he said, VVhat is to me and thee <sc>IESVS</sc> sonne of God most high? I beseech thee doe not torment me.

For he commaunded the vncleane spirit to goe forth out of the man. For many times he caught him, and he was bound vvith chaines, and kept vvith fetters: and breaking the bondes vvas driuen of the deuil into the deserts.
And <sc>IESVS</sc> asked him saying, VVhat is thy name? But he said, Legion. because many deuils vvere entred into him.
And they besought him that he vvould not commaund them to goe into the depth.
And there vvas there a heard of many svvine feeding on the mountaine: and they desired him, that he vvould permit them to enter into them. And he permitted them.
The deuils therfore vvent forth out of the man, and entred into the swine: and the heard vvith violence vvent headlong into the lake, and vvas stifled.
Which vvhen the svvineheards savv done, they fled: and told into the citie and into the townes.

And they vvent forth to see that vvhich vvas done: and they came to <sc>IESVS</sc>, and found the man, out of whom the deuils vvere gone forth, sitting at his feete, clothed, and vvel in his vvittes, and they vvere afraid.
And they also that had seen, told them hovv he had been made whole from the legion.
And al the multitude of the countrie of the Gerasens besought him to depart from them: for they vvere taken vvith great feare. And he going vp into the boate, returned.
And the man out of vvhom the deuils vvere departed, desired him that he might be vvith him. But <sc>IESVS</sc> dimissed him, saying,
Returne into thy house, and tel hovv great things God hath done to thee. And he vvent through the whole citie, preaching hovv great things <sc>IESVS</sc> had done to him.
And it came to passe: when <sc>IESVS</sc> vvas returned, the multitude receiued him. and al vvere expecting him.
And <cr>[1]</cr> behold there came a man vvhose name vvas Iairus, and he vvas Prince of the Synagogue: and he fel at the feete of <sc>IESVS</sc>, desiring him that he vvould enter into his house,
because he had an only daughter almost tvvelue yeres old, and she vvas a dying. And it chaunced, vvhiles he vvent, he vvas thronged of the multitudes.
And there vvas <na>[1]</na> a certaine vvoman in a fluxe of bloud from tvvelue yeres past, vvhich had bestovved al her substance vpon Physicions, neither could she be cured of any:

notes.text: See the Annotations vpon S. Matthew c. 9, 19.

verses.text: she came behind him, and touched the hemme of his garment: and forthvvith the fluxe of her bloud stinted,

And <sc>IESVS</sc> said, VVho is it that touched me? And al denying, <na>[1]</na> Peter said, and they that vvere vvith him, Maister, the multitudes throng and presse thee, and doest thou say, VVho touched me?

notes.text: It is an euident signe of prerogatiue, that Peter only is named so often as cheefe of the company. Mar. 1, 36. Act. 5, 29. Luc. 9, 32. Mar. 16, 7. 1 Cor. 15, 5.

verses.text: And <sc>IESVS</sc> said, Some bodie hath touched me. for I know that there is vertue proceded from me.

And the vvoman seeing, that she vvas not hid, came trembling, and fel dovvne before his feete: and for vvhat cause she had touched him, she shevved before al the people: and hovv forthvvith she vvas made vvhole.
But he said to her, Daughter, thy faith hath made the safe, goe thy vvay in peace.
As he was yet speaking, there commeth one to the Prince of the synagogue, saying to him, That thy daughter is dead, trouble him not.
And <sc>IESVS</sc> hearing this vvord, ansvvered the father of the maide, Feare not: <na>[1]</na> beleeue only, and she shal be safe.

notes.text: See the Annotations vpon S. Marke c. 5, 36.

verses.text: And vvhen he vvas come to the house, he permitted not any man to enter in vvith him, but Peter, and Iames, and Iohn, and the father and mother of the maide.
And al vvept, and mourned for her. But he said, VVeepe not, the maide is not dead, but sleepeth.
And they derided him, knovving that she vvas dead.
But he holding her hand cried saying, Maide arise.
And her spirit returned, and she rose incontinent. And he bade them giue her to eate.
And her parentes were astonied, whom he commaunded to tel no man that which was done.

chapters.summary: Going ouer al Galilee with his traine, 4. he preacheth to the Iewes in parables because of their reprobation: 9. but to his Disciples manifestly: because he wil not for the Iewes incredulity haue his comming frustrate: 19. signifying also that we are his kinne (though we be Gentils) and not his carnal brethren the Iewes. 22. To whom also (signified by the Gerasens) after the tempest in his sleepe (that is, in his death) and caulme in his resurrection, he commeth: but they preferring their temporals before his presence, he leaueth them againe. 41. Likewise comming to cure the Iewes (who were borne when the Gentils sickened, about Abrahams time) he is preuented with the faith of the Gentils, and then the Iewes die. but them also in the end he wil restore.

verses.text: <sc>AND</sc> <cr>[1]</cr><na>[2]</na> calling together the tvvelue Apostles, he gaue them <na>[3]</na> vertue and povver ouer al deuils, and to cure maladies.

notes.text: The Gospel vpon Thursday in whitsonweeke.
To commaund Diuels and diseases either of body or soule, is by nature proper to God onely: but by Gods gift, men also may haue the same. euen so to forgiue sinnes.

verses.text: And he sent them to preach the kingdom of God: and to heale the sicke.
And he said to them, Take nothing for the vvay, neither rod, nor skrippe, nor bread, nor money, neither haue tvvo coates.
And into whatsoeuer house you enter, tarie there, and thence doe not depart.
And whosoever shal not receiue you, going forth out of that citie, shake of the dust also of your feete <na>[1]</na> for a testimonie vpon them.

notes.text: A great fault to reiect the true preachers, or not to admit them into house for needful harbour and sustenance.

verses.text: And going forth they vvent a circuite from tovvne to tovvne euangelizing and curing euery vvhere. ⊢
And <cr>[1]</cr> Herod the Tetrarch heard al things that vvere done by him: and he staggered because it vvas said of some, That Iohn vvas risen from the dead.
but of other some, That Elias hath appeared: and of others, that a Prophet one of the old ones vvas risen.
And Herod said, Iohn I haue beheaded: but vvho is this of vvhom I heare such things? And he sought for to see him.
And <cr>[1]</cr> the Apostles being returned, reported to him vvhatsoeuer they did: and taking them he retired apart into a desert place, vvhich belongeth to Beth-saida.
Which the multitudes vnderstanding, folovved him: & he receiued them, and spake to them of the kingdom of God, and them that had neede of cure he healed.

And the day began to dravv towards an end. And the Tvvelue comming neere, said to him, Dimisse the multitudes, that going into tovvnes and villages here about, they may haue lodging, and finde meates: because here we are in a desert place.
And he said to them, Giue you them to eate. But they said, We haue no more but fiue loaues and tvvo fishes: vnles perhaps vve should goe and bie meates for al this multitude.
And there vvere men almost fiue thousand. And he said to his disciples, Make them sit dovvne by companies fiftie and fiftie.
And so they did. And they made al sit downe.
And taking the fiue loaues and the tvvo fishes, he looked vp vnto heauen, and <na>[1]</na><na>[2]</na> cblessed them: and he brake, and distributed to his disciples, for to set before the multitudes.

notes.text: c εὐλόγησεν αὐτοὺς:
Here you see that he blessed the things, and not only gaue thanks to God. See Annot. Marci. c. 8, 7.

verses.text: And <na>[1]</na> they did al eate, and had their fill. And there vvas taken vp that vvhich remained to them, tvvelue baskets of fragments.

notes.text: The miraculous prouidence. of God toward such as folow Christ into deserts, prisons, banishment, or whithersoeuer.

verses.text: <cr>[1]</cr> And it came to passe: vvhen he vvas alone praying, his disciples also vvere vvith him: and he asked them saying, VVhom doe the multitudes say that I am?
But they answered, and said, Iohn the Baptist: and some, Elias: but some, that one of the Prophets before time, is risen.
And he said to them, But vvhom say ye that I am? Simon Peter ansvvering, said, The <sc>CHRIST</sc> of God.
But he rebuking them, commaunded that they should tell this to no man,
saying, That the sonne of man must suffer many things, and be reiected of the Auncients and cheefe Priests and Scribes, and be killed, and the third day rise againe.
And he said to al, If any man vvil come after me, let him denie him self, and take vp his crosse daily, and folovv me.
For he that vvil saue his life, shal lose it: for he that shal lose his life for my sake, shal saue it.
for vvhat profit hath a man if he gaine the vvhole vvorld, and lose him self, and cast avvay him self?
For he that shal be ashamed of me and of my vvordes, him the Sonne of man shal be ashamed of, vvhen he shal come in his maiestie, and his fathers, and of the holy Angels.
And I say to you assuredly, There be some standing here that shal not tast death, til they see the kingdom of God.
<cr>[1]</cr><na>[2]</na> And it came to passe after these vvordes almost eight daies, and he tooke Peter and Iames and Iohn, and vvent into a mountaine to pray.

notes.text: The TRANSFIGVRATION.

verses.text: And vvhiles he prayed, the shape of his countenance vvas altered: and his raiment vvhite and glistering.
And behold tvvo men talked vvith him. And they vvere Moyses and Elias,
appearing in maiestie. And they told his decease that he should accomplish in Hierusalem.
But Peter and they that vvere vvith him, vvere heauie vvith sleepe. And avvaking, they savv his maiestie, and the tvvo men that stoode vvith him.

And it came to passe, vvhen they departed from him, Peter said to <sc>IESVS</sc>, Maister, it is good for vs to be here: and let vs make three tabernacles, one for thee, and one for Moyses, and one for Elias: not knovving vvhat he said.
And as he spake these things, there came a cloud, and ouershadovved them: and they feared, vvhen they entered into the cloude.
<cr>[1]</cr> And a voice vvas made out of the cloude, saying, This is my beloued sonne, heare him.
And vvhiles the voice vvas made, <sc>IESVS</sc> vvas found alone. And they held their peace, and told no man in those daies any of these things vvhich they had seen.
<cr>[1]</cr> And it came to passe the day folovving, vvhen they came dovvne from the mountaine, there mette him a great multitude.
And behold a man of the multitude cried out, saying, Maister, I beseeche thee, looke vpon my sonne because he is mine only one.
and loe, the spirit taketh him, and he sodenly crieth, and he dasheth him, and teareth him that he fometh, and vvith much a doe departeth renting him.
And I desired thy disciples to cast him out, and they could not.
And <sc>IESVS</sc> ansvvering said, <na>[1]</na> O faithles and peruerse generation, how long shal I be with you and suffer you? bring hither thy sonne.

notes.text: Incredulitie hindereth the effect of Exorcismes, and other miraculous power giuen to the Church.

verses.text: And vvhen he came to him, the deuil dashed, and tore him. And <sc>IESVS</sc> rebuked the vncleane spirit, and healed the lad: and rendred him to his father.
And al were astonied at the might of God: and al merueiling at al things that he did, he said to his disciples,
Lay you in your hartes these vvordes, for it shal come to passe that the Sonne of man shal be deliuered into the hands of men.
But they did not know this vvord, and it vvas couered before them, that they perceiued it not. And they vvere afraid to aske him of this vvord.
<cr>[1]</cr> And there entred <na>[2]</na> a cogitation into them, vvhich of them should be greater.

notes.text: Desire of preeminence is an humane infirmitie often euen among the good. Against which, Christ teacheth humility, but forbiddeth not Superiority.

verses.text: But <sc>IESVS</sc> seeing the cogitations of their hart, tooke a childe and set him by him,
and said to them, Whosoeuer receiueth this childe in my name, receiueth me: and vvhosoeuer receiueth me, receiueth him that sent me. For he that is the lesser among you al, he is the greater.
<cr>[1]</cr> And Iohn ansvvering said, Maister, vve savv a certaine man casting out deuils in thy name, and vve prohibited him, because he folovveth not vvith vs.
And <sc>IESVS</sc> said to him, <na>[1]</na> Prohibit not. for he that is not against you, is for you.

notes.text: There be some that folow not Christ precisely in life and doctrine, of whom we may make our aduantage to the propagation of Christes honour and religion, when they doe any thing for the aduancement thereof, of what intention soeuer they doe it. Philip. 1, 15.

verses.text: And it came to passe, vvhiles the daies of his assumption were accomplishing, and he fixed his face to goe into Hierusalem.
And he sent messengers before his face: and going they entred into a citie of the Samaritans to prepare for him.
And they receiued him not, because his face vvas to goe to Hierusalem.
And vvhen his disciples Iames and Iohn had seen it, they said, Lord vvilt thou vve say that fire come dovvne from heauen and consume <na>[1]</na> <alt>`them</alt>'?

notes.text: `them as Elias also did?

verses.text: And turning, he rebuked them, saying, You knovv not of vvhat spirit you are.
The sonne of man came not to destroy soules, but to saue. And they vvent into an other tovvne.
And it came to passe as they vvalked in the vvay, a certaine man said to him, <cr>[1]</cr> I vvil folovv thee vvhithersoeuer thou goest.
<sc>IESVS</sc> said to him, <na>[1]</na> The foxes haue holes, and the foules of the aire nestes: but the sonne of man hath not where to repose his head.

notes.text: This man would haue folowed him for temporal commodities, and therfore was not suffered.

verses.text: But he said to an other, Folow me. And he said, Lord, permit me first to goe, and to burie my father.
And <sc>IESVS</sc> said to him, Let the dead burie their dead: but goe thou, set forth the kingdom of God.
And an other said, I vvil folovv thee Lord, but permit me first to take my leaue of them that are at home.
<sc>IESVS</sc> said to him, No man putting his hand to the plough, and looking backe, is apt for the kingdom of God.

chapters.summary: His Twelue also now preaching euery where and working miracles. 6. Herod and al do wonder much. 10. After which, he taketh them and goeth into the wildernesse: where he cureth and teacheth, feeding 5000 with fiue loaues. 18. Peter confessing him to be Christ, 21. he on the other side foretelleth his Passion, and that al must in time of persecution folow him therein. 27. Wherevnto to encourage vs the more, 27. he giueth in his Transfiguration a sight of the glorie, which is the reward of suffering. 37. The next day he casteth out a diuel which his Disciples could not. 43. Whom amiddes these wonders he forewarneth againe of his scandalous Passion. 49. And to cure their ambition, he telleth them, that the most humble he esteemeth most: 49. bidding them also, not to prohibit any that is not against them. 51. Yea and toward such as be against them Schismatically, to shew mildnes for al that. 57. Of folowing him, three examples.

verses.text: <sc>AND</sc> <na>[1]</na> after this our Lord designed also other <na>[2]</na> seuentie tvvo: and he sent them tvvo and tvvo before his face into euery citie and place vvhither him self vvould come.

notes.text: The Gospel upon S. Mark's day. April. 25. and S. Luke's Octob. 18.
As the twelue Apostles did represent the higher degree of the clergie, called Bishops: so these Seuentie two beare the figure of the inferiour clergie, called Priests. Beda.

verses.text: And he said to them, The haruest truely is much: but the vvorkemen fevv. Desire therfore the lord of the haruest, that he send vvorkemen into his haruest.
Goe: behold I send you as lambes among wolues.
Carie not purse nor skrip, nor shoes: and salute no body by the vvay.
Into vvhatsoeuer house you enter, first say, Peace to this house.
and if the sonne of peace be there, your peace shal rest vpon him: but if not, it shal returne to you.
And in the same house tarie you, eating and drinking such things as they haue. <cr>[1]</cr> For the vvorkeman is vvorthie of his hire. Remoue not from house to house.
And into vvhat citie soeuer you enter, and they receiue you, eate such things as are set before you:
and cure the sicke that are in it, and say to them, The kingdom of God is come nigh vpon you. ⊢
And into vvhatsoeuer citie you enter, and they receiue you not, going forth into the streates thereof, say,
The dust also of your citie that cleaueth to vs, vve doe vvipe of against you. yet this knovv ye that the kingdom of God is at hand.
I say to you, it shal be <na>[1]</na> more tolerable for Sodom in that day, then for that citie.

notes.text: Differences of paines and damnation in Hel according to the differences of demerites. Aug. li. 5. c. 5. cont. Iulian.

verses.text: VVo to thee Corozáim, vvo to thee Beth-saida: for if in Tyre and Sidon had been vvrought the miracles that haue beene vvrought in you, they had done penance sitting <na>[1]</na> in sacke cloth and ashes long agoe.

notes.text: True penance not onely to lead a new life, but to punish the body by such things as here be recorded, for the il life past.

verses.text: But it shal be more tolerable for Tyre and Sidon in the iudgement, then for you.
And thou Capharnaum that art exalted vnto heauen: thou shalt be thrust dovvne euen vnto hel.
<na>[1]</na><na>[2]</na> He that heareth you, heareth me: and he that despiseth you, despiseth me. And he that despiseth me, despiseth him that sent me.

notes.text: The Gospel for many Martyrs.
It is al one to despise Christ, and to despise his Priests and Ministers in the the Catholike Church: to refuse his doctrine, & theirs.

verses.text: And the Seuentie-tvvo returned vvith ioy, saying, Lord, the Deuils also are subiect to vs in thy name.
And he said to them, I savv Satan as a lightening fal from heauen.
Behold, I haue giuen you povver to treade vpon serpents, and scorpions, and vpon al the povver of the enemie, and nothing shal hurt you.
But yet reioyce not in this, that the spirits are subiect vnto you: but reioyce in this, that your names are written in heauen. ⊢

In that very houre he reioyced in spirit, and said, I confesse to thee O Father, Lord of heauen and earth, because thou hast hid these things from the wise and prudent, and hast reuealed them to litle ones. Yea Father, for so hath it wel pleased thee.
Al things are deliuered to me of my father. And no man knovveth vvho the Sonne is, but the Father: and vvho the Father is, but the Sonne, and to vvhom the Sonne vvil reueale.
And turning to his Disciples, he said, Blessed are the eies that see the things that you see.
<na>[1]</na> For I say to you, that many Prophets and Kings desired to see the things that you see, and saw them not: and to heare the things that you heare, and heard them not.

notes.text: The Gospel vpon the 12 Sunday after Pentecost.

verses.text: And behold a certaine lawyer stoode vp, tempting him and saying, Maister, by doing of what thing shal I possesse life euerlasting?
But he said to him, In the law what is written? how readest thou?
He answering said, [1] Thou shalt loue the Lord thy God with thy whole hart, and with thy whole soule, and with al thy strength, and with al thy minde: and thy neighbour as thy self. [2]
And he said to him, Thou hast answered right, this doe and thou shalt liue.
But he desirous to iustifie him self, said to <sc>IESVS</sc>, And who is my neighbour?
And <sc>IESVS</sc> taking it, said, A certaine man went downe from Hierusalem into Iericho, and fel among theeues, who also spoiled him, and giuing him woundes went away leauing him halfe-dead.
And it chaunced that a certaine Priest went downe the same way: and seeing him, passed by.
In like maner also a Leuite, when he was neere the place, and saw him, passed by.
But a certaine Samaritane going his iourney, came neere him: and seeing him, was moued with mercie.
And going vnto him, bound his woundes, powring in oile and wine: and setting him vpon his owne beast, brought him into an inne, and tooke care of him.
And the next day he tooke forth two pence, and gaue to the host, and said, Haue care of him: and whatsoeuer thou shalt <na>[1]</na><na>[2]</na> supererogate, I at my returne wil repay thee.

notes.text: S. Augustin saith that the Apostle (1. Cor. 9.) according to this place did supererogate, that is, did more then he needed or was bound to doe, when he might haue required al duties for preaching the Gospel, but would not. li. de op. Monach. c. 5. whereof it commeth, that the workes which we doe more then precept, be called workes of Supererogation: & whereby it is also euident against the Protestants, that there be such workes. See Optatus li. 6 cont. Parmen. how aptly he applyeth this parable to S. Paules counsel of virginitie (1 Cor. 7) as to a worke of supererogation.
Supererogaveris, προσδαπανήσῃς,

verses.text: Which of these three in thy opinion was neighbour to him that fel among theeues?
But he said, He that did mercie vpon him. And <sc>IESVS</sc> said to him, Goe, and doe thou in like maner. ⊢
b <na>[1]</na> And it came to passe as they went, and he entred into a certaine towne: and a certaine woman named Martha, receiued him into her house,

notes.text: b the Gospel upon the Assumption of our B. Lady. Aug. 15. And in the feast of S. Martha. Iulij. 29.

verses.text: and she had a sister called Marie. who sitting also at our Lords feete, heard his word.
But Martha was busie about much seruice. who stoode and said, Lord, hast thou no care that my sister hath left me alone to serue? speake to her therfore, that she help me.
And our Lord answering said to her, Martha, Martha, thou art careful, and art troubled about very many things.
But one thing is necessarie. Marie hath chosen the best part which shal not be taken away from her. ⊢

chapters.summary: He sendeth yet 72. moe to preach to the Iewes, with power also of miracles, 13. crying wo to the cities impenitent. 17. At their returne he agniseth the great power he gaue them, but yet teacheth them not to be proud thereof, 21. and praiseth God for his grace, 23. his Church also for her happy state. 25. To one of the Scribes he sheweth, that the loue of God and of his neighbour wil bring him to life euerlasting, 29. teaching him by the parable of the Samaritane, to take euery one for his neighbour that needeth his charitie. 38. To Martha he sheweth that Maries Contemplatiue life is the better.

verses.text: <sc>AND</sc> it came to passe, vvhen he was in a certaine place, praying, as he ceased, one of his Disciples said to him, Lord teach vs to pray, as Iohn also taught his Disciples.
And he said to them, [1] VVhen you pray, say, FATHER, sanctified be thy name. Thy kingdom come,
Our daily bread giue vs this day,
and forgiue vs our sinnes, for because our selues also doe forgiue euery one that is in debt to vs. And lead vs not into temptation.
<na>[1]</na> And he said to them, VVhich of you shal haue a frende, and shal goe to him at midnight, and shal say to him, Frende, lend me three loaues,

notes.text: The Gospel in Maioribus Litanijs on S. Markes day, and in the Rogation daies. And in a votiue Masse against the Pagans.

verses.text: because a frende of mine is come out of his way to me, and I haue not what to set before him:
& he from within ansvvering saith, Trouble me not, novv the doore is shut, and my children are vvith me in bed: I can not rise and giue thee.
And if he shal perseuêre knocking, I say to you, although he vvil not rise and giue him because he is his frende, yet for his importunitie he vvil rise, and giue him as many as he needeth.
<cr>[1]</cr><na>[2]</na> And I say to you, Aske, and it shal be giuen you: seeke, and you shal finde: knocke, and it shal be opened to you.

notes.text: The Gospel in a votiue Masse for sinnes.

verses.text: For euery one that asketh, receiueth: and he that seeketh, findeth: and to him that knocketh, it shal be opened.
And vvhich of you if he aske his father bread, vvil he giue him a stone? or a fish, vvil he for a fish giue him a serpent?
Or if he aske an egge, vvil he reach him a scorpion?
If you then being naught, knovv hovv to giue good giftes to your children, hovv much more vvil your father from heauen giue the good spirit to them that aske him? ⊢
<cr>[1]</cr> And he vvas casting out a deuil, and that vvas dumme. And vvhen he had cast out the deuil, the dumme spake: and the multitudes marueiled.
<cr>[1]</cr><na>[2]</na> And certaine of them said, In Beel-zebub the prince of Deuils he casteth out Deuils.

notes.text: Mt. 12, 22. · The Gospel vpon the 3 Sunday in Lent.

verses.text: And other tempting, asked of him a signe from heauen.
But he seeing their cogitations, said to them, Euery kingdom deuided against it self, shal be made desolate, and c <na>[1]</na> house vpon house, shal fall.

notes.text: c ὀῖκος ἐπὶ ὀῖκον

verses.text: And if Satan also be deuided against him self, hovv shal his kingdom stand? because you say that in Beel-zebub I doe cast out Deuils.
And if I in Beel-zebub cast out Deuils: your children, in vvhom doe they cast out? therfore they shal be your iudges.
But if I in the <na>[1]</na> finger of God doe cast out Deuils: surely the kingdom of God is come vpon you.

notes.text: This finger, is the spirit of God, Mt. 12, 28.

verses.text: When the strong armed keepeth his court: those things are in peace that he possesseth.
But if a stronger then he, come vpon him and ouercome him: he vvil take avvay his vvhole armour vvherein he trusted, and vvil distribute his spoiles.
He that is not vvith me, is against me: and he that gathereth not vvith me, scattereth.
When the vncleane spirit shal depart out of a man, he vvandereth through places vvithout vvater, seeking rest. And not finding, he saith, I vvil returne into my house vvhence I departed.
And when he is come, he findeth it swept vvith a besome, and trimmed.
Then he goeth and taketh seuen other spirits vvorse then him self, and entring in they dvvel there. And the c <na>[1]</na> last of that man be made vvorse then the first.

notes.text: nouissima fiunt

verses.text: b <na>[1]</na> And it came to passe: vvhen he said these things, a certaine vvoman lifting vp her voice out of the multitude said to him, Blessed is the vvombe that bare thee, and the pappes that thou didst sucke.

notes.text: The Gospel vpon Assumption eue, and in a Votiue of our Lady betwene Candlemas and Easter, and betwene Pentecost and Aduent.

verses.text: But he said, <na>[1]</na> Yea rather, blessed are they that heare the vvord of God, and keepe it. ⊢

notes.text: The said mother of God, in that also was blessed that she was the temporal meanes & minister of the Incarnation, but much more blessed, in that she continued the perpetual keeper of his word. Beda. Aug. tract. 19. in Ioan.

verses.text: And the multitudes running together, he began to say, <cr>[1]</cr> This generation, is a vvicked generation: it asketh a signe, and a signe shal not be giuen it but the signe of Ionas the Prophet.
<cr>[1]</cr> For as Ionas vvas a signe to the Niniuites: so shal the Sonne of man also be to this generation.

<cr>[1]</cr> The Queene of the South shal rise in the iudgement vvith the men of this generation, and shal condemne them: because she came from the endes of the earth to heare the vvisedom of Salomon. and behold, more then Salomon here.

The men of Niniuee shal rise in the iudgement vvith this generation, and shal condemne it, <cr>[1]</cr> because they <na>[2]</na> did penance at the preaching of Ionas. and behold, more then Ionas here.

notes.text: μετενόησαν. Marke that the great penance of the Niniuites (Ionae 3) is here expressed by this Greeke word. See Annot. Mat. 3, 2.

verses.text: <cr>[1]</cr><na>[2]</na> No man lighteth a candel, and putteth it in secrete, neither vnder a bushel: but vpon a candlesticke, that they that goe in may see the light.

notes.text: The Gospel upon S. Martin's day. Novem. 11. & for some other Confessors Bishops.

verses.text: <cr>[1]</cr> The candel of thy body, is thine eie. If thine eie be simple, thy vvhole body shal be lightsome: but if it be naught, thy body also shal be darkesome.
See therfore that the light vvhich is in thee, be not darkenesse.
If then thy vvhole body be lightsome, hauing no part of darkenesse: it shal be lightsome vvholy, and as a bright candel it shal lighten thee. ⊢
And vvhen he vvas speaking, a certaine Pharisee desired him that he vvould dine vvith him. and he going in sate dovvne to eate.
And the Pharisee began to thinke vvithin him self and to say, VVhy he vvas not vvashed before dinner.
And our Lord said to him, <cr>[1]</cr> Novv you Pharisees doe make cleane that on the out side of the cuppe and of the platter: but that of yours vvhich is vvithin, is ful of rapine and iniquitie.
Fooles, did not he that made that on the outside, make that also that is on the inside?
But yet c <na>[1]</na> that that remaineth, giue almes, & behold al things are cleane vnto you.

notes.text: Quod superest, τὰ ἐνόντα,

verses.text: But vvo to you Pharisees, because you tithe minte and revve and euery herbe: and passe ouer iudgement and the charitie of God. but these things you ought to haue done, and not to omit those.
Wo to you Pharisees, because you loue the first chaires in the synagogs, and salutations in the market-place.
Wo to you, because you are as monuments that appeare not, and men walking ouer, are not vvare.
And one of the Lavvyers answering saith to him, Maister, in saying these things, thou speakest to our reproche also.
But he said, Wo to you Lavvyers also: because you lode men vvith burdens which they can not beare, and your selues touch not the packes vvith one of your fingers.
<na>[1]</na> Wo to you that <na>[2]</na> build the monuments of the Prophets: and your fathers did kil them.

notes.text: The Gospel for many Martyrs.
Not the building of the Prophets monuments is condemned, but their imitation of their fathers that slew the Prophets. Ambros.

verses.text: Surely you doe testifie that you consent to the vvorkes of your fathers: because they in deede did kil them, and you build their sepulchres.
For this cause the wisedom also of God said, I vvil send to them Prophets and Apostles, and of them they vvil kil and persecute.
that the bloud of al the Prophets that vvas shed from the making of the vvorld, may be required of this generation,
<cr>[1]</cr> from the bloud of Abel vnto the <cr>[2]</cr> bloud of Zacharie that vvas slaine betvvene the altar and the temple. Yea I say to you, it shal be required of this generation. ⊢
Vvo to you Lavvyers, because you haue taken avvay the key of knovvledge: your selues haue not entred, and those that did enter you haue prohibited.
And vvhen he said these things to them, the Pharisees and the Lavvyers began vehemently to vrge him, and to stoppe his mouth about many things,
lying in waite for him, & seeking to catch some thing of his mouth, that they might accuse him.

chapters.summary: He teacheth a forme of prayer, 5. and exhorteth to pray instantly, 11. assuring that so God wil giue vs good things. 14. The Iewes blaspheming his casting out of Diuels, and asking for a miracle from heauen, 17. he defendeth his doing: 22. foretelling also the Diuels expulsion by him out of the world (that is, the vocation of the Gentils) 24. and his reentrie into their nation, 27. with their reprobation though he be of their flesh, 29. and also their final most worthy damnation. 37. Againe, to the Pharisees and Scribes he crieth wo, as authors of the said reprobation now at hand.

verses.text: <sc>AND</sc> <na>[1]</na> when great multitudes stoode about him, so that they trode one an other, he began to say to his Disciples, Take good heede of the leauen of the Pharisees, vvhich is hypocrisie.

notes.text: The Gospel upon SS. John and Paul's day, Iunij 26. And for many other Martyrs.

verses.text: <cr>[1]</cr> For nothing is hid, that shal not be reuealed: nor secrete, that shal not be knovven.
For the things that you haue said in darknesse, shal be said in the light: and that which you haue spoken into the eare in the chambers, shal be preached in the house-toppes.
And I say to you my frendes, Be not afraid of them that kil the body, and after this haue no more to doe.
But I wil shew you whom ye shal feare: <na>[1]</na> feare him vvho after he hath killed, hath povver to cast into hel. yea I say to you, feare him.

notes.text: The feare of Hel also is profitable: contrarie to the protestants, teaching securitie of saluation, and that feare of Hel maketh men hypocrites.

verses.text: Are not fiue sparowes sold for tvvo farthings: and one of them is not forgotten before God?
Yea the heares also of your head are al numbered. Feare not therfore: you are more vvorth then many sparowes.
<cr>[1]</cr> And I say to you, Euery one that confesseth me before men, the Sonne of man also vvil confesse him before the Angels of God.
But he that denieth me before men, shal be denied before the Angels of God.
<cr>[1]</cr> And <cr>[2]</cr> euery one that speaketh a vvord against the sonne of man, it shal be forgiuen him: but he that shal blaspheme against the holy Ghost, to him it shal not be forgiuen.
<cr>[1]</cr> And vvhen they shal bring you in to the synagogs and to magistrates and potestates, be not careful in what maner, and vvhat you shal ansvver, or vvhat you shal say.
For the holy Ghost shal teach you in the very houre vvhat you must say.
And one of the multitude said to him, Maister, speake to my brother that he deuide the inheritaunce vvith me.
But he said to him, Man, vvho hath appointed me iudge or deuider ouer you?
And he said to them, See and bevvare of al auarice: for not in any mans aboundance doth his life consist, of those things vvhich he possesseth.
And he spake a similitude to them, saying, A certaine riche mans field yelded plentie of fruites.
